correctness.summary: A local nonnegative-difference inequality bounds each vertex contribution; summation reduces RAlb(T) to twice a weighted edge sum. Bipartiteness bounds that edge sum by a product of the two part-weight sums, whose total is n-2. Equality forces the connected non-leaf core to be exactly one edge, hence a double star, and balancing its two leaf counts gives the unique maximizer for n>=4. Exhaustive checks of all non-isomorphic trees through n=17 agree.

limitations: Unindexed or differently named equivalent results remain a residual originality risk.
No exact extension to unicyclic or general connected graphs is claimed.
Finite verification through order 17 is supporting evidence only.
Independent audit has not been performed.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The 1997 Albertson framework, line-graph/composite-graph literature, the 2025 paper introducing RAlb and identifying RAlb(G)=Alb(L(G)), and recent ordinary-Albertson extremal work were checked. Searches under reformulated-Albertson, line-graph irregularity, exact-formula and balanced-double-star formulations found no sharp order-only tree maximum or equivalent equality characterization. The directly relevant 2025 paper gives general parameter upper bounds rather than this theorem.

value.summary: The result gives an exact order-only maximum and unique extremal tree for a newly introduced edge irregularity index, and equivalently determines the maximum Albertson irregularity among line graphs of trees. It substantially sharpens broad parameter-dependent bounds on this class.
